skill: Infer rank and nullity from pivot/non-pivot counts or an explicitly parametrized/spanned null space, apply rank-nullity and the square invertible matrix theorem, and evaluate three statements.
learner_operation: Determine the dimension of the supplied null space or pivot count; derive the complementary rank/nullity; decide each statement independently and select the corresponding subset.
reasoning_steps: Identify n, the number of columns.
Extract rank from pivot columns or nullity from non-pivot columns / independent null-space generators.
Use invertibility iff rank=n iff nullity=0; connect column-space dimension and determinant zero.
Evaluate all three claims and express the subset through the supplied radio bank or three checkbox truth fields.
response_contract: Radio questions use complete five-choice banks of subsets of I/II/III; checkbox questions have three statement keys and true/false choices per field. Preserve each source bank during replay. Canonical example has no captured answer fields: its solution specifies I only.
difficulty: Moderate source includes direct counts and low-complexity parametric null spaces; hard includes explicit span and some larger parametrizations. Avoid introducing matrix elimination, nonlinear parameters, determinant calculation, or proof workload.
invariants: A is square when using invertibility equivalences.
All null-space vectors have n entries; nullity is span dimension, not blindly number of parameters.
Every statement and worked explanation must be derived from the supplied data.
Keep three truth judgments and source response shapes.
permitted_variations: n and pivot/non-pivot count, including full-rank and zero-rank boundaries if clearly expressed with the same method.
Null-space coefficients, signs, coordinate locations, and independent directions without adding elimination workload.
Numerical claims of rank/nullity/column dimension and whether they match the derived values.
Statement polarity and order, subset of true statements, labels and choice positions; none is mathematically fixed by the theorem.
Radio distractor subsets may vary provided the true subset appears uniquely and replay banks remain exact.

fixed_features.justification: The source applies invertibility equivalences for n by n matrices.
Observed evaluation workload and response shape.
